title: Drying Science, Moisture Migration, Water Activity & Environment
level: Postharvest Quality Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the Postharvest Quality Specialist pathway
Postharvest and quality personnel responsible for controlled product evidence, traceability and escalation
prerequisites: Cultivation Technician II harvest/postharvest foundation or equivalent
COURSE-LH-PHQ-001 or equivalent controlled harvest/lot-integrity foundation
evidencePolicy: Course uses cannabis-specific peer-reviewed postharvest evidence plus authoritative quality, measurement and traceability sources. Research treatments, standards and transferable quality models remain within source scope and do not become universal facility setpoints or jurisdiction-specific legal requirements.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize product release, rejection, destruction, laboratory disposition, recall execution or jurisdiction-specific compliance decisions outside assigned authority.
description: Develops specialist interpretation of drying as a coupled heat-and-mass-transfer process, representative product measurement, dry-room mapping, endpoint evidence and controlled response to nonuniform or interrupted drying.
learningOutcomes: Analyze how product geometry, load density, temperature, humidity and airflow interact to create drying rate and spatial moisture gradients.
Distinguish moisture content from water activity and evaluate how sampling, equilibration, method and instrument condition limit interpretation.
Design a dry-room monitoring map that distinguishes sensor readings from product exposure and tests airflow and load-distribution assumptions.
Evaluate drying endpoint evidence using representative locations, time trends, product objectives and predefined decision authority.
Construct a drying-deviation response that preserves event facts, affected scope, product evidence, interim controls and accountable handoff.
